AssertAction.description: Fail the flow unless a condition holds: exactly one of the two fields is set.

human.description: Perform the step the way a person would (mouse path, key cadence); default true.

timeout_ms.description: Budget for this step in milliseconds; default 30000.

BehaviorMode.description: What kind of visit a navigation is. `human`: the persona at its mouse and keyboard, as the other fields of the behavior say. `still`: the persona's browser loads the page and nothing else: no input at all (no pointer, no wheel, no key), a typed entry, the fixed dwell `dwell_ms`, no scrolling, no wandering, no patience. A page sees of it what it sees of a visitor whose hand rests.

seed.description: Seed of this request. With the persona's own seed it decides every movement; the same pair replays the same behavior. Absent: the sidecar draws one and returns it.

mode.description: What kind of visit this is; default `human`. `still`: a visit that sends no input at all (no pointer, no wheel, no key), arrives by a typed navigation (`entry` absent, `direct` or `none`), dwells for the fixed `dwell_ms`, and neither scrolls, wanders nor waits with patience; a request that also names `scroll_depth`, `patience_ms`, `wander: true`, `dwell: human`, an entry by `link` or `search_engine`, or `from_open_page: true` is refused. Its report has the seed, the profile of the persona, the entry, the dwell, and every count 0. Since 1.5.0.

entry.description: How the target is arrived at; default a typed navigation.

scroll_depth.description: Scroll down to this share of the document with the wheel, a flick at a time, resting after each as long as the text in view takes the persona to skim. Absent: no scrolling.

dwell.description: Where the dwell time comes from; default `fixed`.

wander.description: Move the mouse a little now and then while dwelling, as an idle hand does; default true, and never in a `still` visit.

patience_ms.description: How long the persona goes on scrolling this page at most. With it, `timeout_ms` of the request bounds reaching the page only (the navigation, its waits, the challenge wait): the scrolling ends at `scroll_depth` or when the patience is used up, whichever comes first, and the dwell follows in full. Whoever asks draws it anew for every page, so that no two long pages are left after the same time. Absent: the scrolling and the dwell share what `timeout_ms` leaves, as before 1.3.0, and every page too long for that is left at the same moment.

BehaviorOptions.description: What a persona does on a page besides loading it. All input is sent through the mouse and keyboard of the context's own display; a `still` visit sends none and is reported all the same. Absent from a request: no input at all, a bare page load.

seed.description: The seed of this request: the one given, or the one the sidecar drew.

profile_id.description: Identifies the motor profile of the persona: the same for every request of one persona.

entry.description: What the entry did; null when the request named none.

dwell_ms.description: Time spent dwelling: on the page of a navigation, or on all the pages a paced flow arrived on together.

positions.description: Positions the mouse reported during them.

overshoots.description: Movements that went past their target and came back.

keys.description: Keys pressed, modifiers and corrections included.

patience_ms.description: The patience the request gave the scrolling; null when it gave none.

scroll_reached.description: How far down the document the page was when the scrolling of a navigation ended, as a share of its scrollable height: 0 at the top, 1 at the end, and 1 for a document that ends inside its window; null when no scrolling was asked for, and for a flow.

scroll_ended_by.description: Why that scrolling ended; null when no scrolling was asked for, and for a flow.

BehaviorReport.description: What the behavior engine did during a request. With the persona and this seed the behavior can be replayed.

BodyEncoding.description: How a captured body is written: as text, or base64 when it is not valid UTF-8.

dom.description: The document as HTML after the wait settled.

raw.description: The body of the main response as the server sent it, decoded.

xhr.description: XHR and fetch() responses to keep; null for none.

console.description: Log entries the engine can collect without a page noticing. On chromium: what the browser itself logs (failed loads, security and deprecation messages); `console.*` calls and uncaught exceptions are not available there, because reading them needs a debugger domain that pages can detect. On firefox: the page's `console.*` calls and uncaught errors.

links.description: The links of the document, each with whether a reader can see it and whether it stands in what the site repeats on every page. Read in the isolated world, like the document; the page cannot notice. Default false.

bytes.description: Size of the whole decoded body in bytes.

truncated.description: Whether `data` holds less than the whole body.

data.description: The body, or its first part when truncated.

vendors.description: Vendors whose scripts, frames or markers were seen, for example `cloudflare`.

script_hosts.description: Hosts of every script the page requested, sorted.

iframe_hosts.description: Hosts of every frame the page embedded, sorted.

interstitial.description: Whether the first document looked like a challenge page and not like content.

marker.description: The marker that identified the interstitial; null without one.

resolved.description: Whether the interstitial went away by itself within the wait; null when there was none.

waited_ms.description: How long the interstitial was waited for.

ChallengeSignals.description: What a page shows of bot-protection vendors. Signals only; Kage classifies.

ClaimedOs.description: The operating system a persona claims to run.

human.description: Perform the step the way a person would (mouse path, key cadence); default true.

timeout_ms.description: Budget for this step in milliseconds; default 30000.

ConsoleCapture.description: What the console list holds. `browser_log`: entries the engine collected without the page noticing (chromium: the browser's own log; firefox: console calls and uncaught errors of the page). `unsupported`: the engine cannot read any log without becoming detectable. `not_requested`: the request did not ask.

source.description: Where the browser says it came from: `network`, `security`, `deprecation`, ...

url.description: The resource it is about; null when unknown.

ConsoleEntry.description: One entry the browser itself logged about a page.

ConsoleLevel.description: Severity of a browser log entry.

domain.description: The host that set the cookie, or its `Domain` attribute. Lower case, no leading dot.

host_only.description: True when the cookie had no `Domain` attribute and goes to exactly `domain`.

path.description: The path the cookie is sent under.

same_site.description: The `SameSite` attribute; null when the cookie carried none, which browsers treat as `lax`.

expires_at.description: When the cookie expires; null for a session cookie.

Cookie.description: One cookie, with the fields of a row of Kage's `http_cookies` table.

CookieRejection.description: Why a cookie was not imported. `foreign_domain`: it does not belong to the origin. `expired`: its expiry is in the past. `refused_by_browser`: the browser's own cookie rules refused it.

DwellMode.description: Where the dwell time comes from. `fixed`: `dwell_ms` of the request. `human`: drawn from the persona's own distribution (log-normal, median about 6 s, at most 45 s), never longer than the budget allows.

ja4.description: The JA4 of the browser's TLS ClientHello.

akamai.description: The HTTP/2 fingerprint in Akamai's notation.

headers.description: The header names of a typed navigation, in wire order.

EchoExpectation.description: What the fingerprint echo must report for this browser: the capture recorded in `tests/fixtures/fingerprints/browser/`.

EngineName.description: A browser engine. One sidecar container runs exactly one.

from_url.description: The page to start from: required for `link` and `search_engine`, ignored otherwise. For `search_engine` it is the results URL Kage built from its policy template.

fallback.description: What to do without a link to the target; default `stop`.

from_open_page.description: Only with `link`. True: `from_url` is a page the persona has been reading, and nothing is loaded to start from. When it is the page that is open, its link to the target is clicked there. When it is one of the `max_backs` pages before it in the tab, the persona goes back to it with the keyboard first (the browser's own way back: no request when the browser kept the page) and clicks there. When the tab does not hold it, or it holds no such link, `fallback` decides; a link no reader could click there (one that is not rendered, lies under something else, or opens another tab) is none. The report says how many entries back the page was. Default false.

max_backs.description: With `from_open_page`: how many entries of the tab the persona goes back at most to find `from_url`; default 0, the open page only.

Entry.description: How a navigation arrives at its target.

EntryFallback.description: What to do when the link or result is not there. `stop`: load nothing else and say so. `none`: load the target as a typed navigation.

EntryOutcome.description: How an entry ended. `arrived`: the target was reached the way the strategy says. `fell_back`: no link was there and the target was loaded as a typed navigation instead. `link_not_found`, `result_not_found`: no link or result led to the target and nothing else was loaded. `blocked`: the page to start from did not load or showed a wall; nothing was typed into it.

strategy.description: The strategy that was asked for.

from_url.description: The page the entry started from; null for a typed navigation.

referer.description: The `Referer` the browser sent with the request for the target; null when it sent none.

backs.description: With `from_open_page`: how many entries the persona went back in the tab before it clicked, 0 when the page that was open held the link; null for every other entry, and when the target was not reached by a click.

EntryReport.description: How a navigation arrived at its target.

EntryStrategy.description: How the target is arrived at. `none` and `direct`: a typed navigation, with no `Referer`, `Sec-Fetch-Site: none` and `Sec-Fetch-User: ?1`; the two names are equal on the wire. `link`: the link to the target is found on `from_url` and clicked; `from_url` is loaded as a typed navigation first or, with `from_open_page`, looked for in the tab. `search_engine`: `from_url` is a results page; the first result that leads to the target's host is clicked. A referer is never forged: it is whatever the browser sends for the click.

ErrorCode.description: Stable error code of a refused or failed request. `unauthorized`: the shared secret is missing or wrong. `invalid_request`: the body, a parameter or the URL does not match the contract. `not_found`: no such route. `context_not_found`: no open context has this id. `context_limit`: the container already runs its maximum number of contexts. `context_conflict`: the persona has an open context that was opened with different parameters. `context_busy`: the context is running another operation. `cross_os_claim_disabled`: the engine may only claim the operating system it runs on. `browser_major_mismatch`: the request names a browser major the engine does not bundle. `browser_launch_failed`: the browser or its display did not start. `not_implemented`: the engine does not implement this endpoint yet. `payload_too_large`: the request body is over the limit. `internal`: an unexpected failure, see the logs.

code.description: What went wrong, as a stable code.

message.description: A sentence for the log. Never parse it.

ErrorResponse.description: Body of every answer that is not a success.

claimed_os.description: The operating system the persona claims.

browser_major.description: The browser major the persona presents.

languages.description: The persona's languages, most preferred first.

ExpectedIdentity.description: The identity a self-test expects to see.

origin.description: The origin whose state is exported, for example `https://example.org`.

ExportStateRequest.description: Which state to export from a context.

origin.description: The origin that was asked for.

cookies.description: Every cookie the browser would send to that origin, session cookies included.

local_storage.description: The origin's `localStorage`; null when not requested, or when the context's page is on another origin and the storage cannot be read without loading something.

session_storage.description: The origin's `sessionStorage`, under the same conditions.

ExportStateResponse.description: Cookies and storage of one origin.

human.description: Perform the step the way a person would (mouse path, key cadence); default true.

timeout_ms.description: Budget for this step in milliseconds; default 30000.

ExtractAction.description: Capture the page at this point of the flow.

page.description: The id of the page the check ran on.

check.description: Name of the check, stable per page kind.

hard.description: Whether a `fail` here fails the whole self-test: an automation flag, an identity mismatch or a transport mismatch.

weight.description: Weight of the check in the score.

observed.description: What the page showed; null when nothing was read.

expected.description: What was expected; null when the check has no fixed expectation.

Finding.description: One check of a self-test and its verdict.

FindingStatus.description: Verdict of one check. `unknown`: the page could not be reached or read; it changes no score.

FlowAction.description: One step of a flow, chosen by `action`.

seed.description: Seed of this flow. With the persona's own seed it decides every movement, key and pause; absent: the sidecar draws one and returns it.

typos.description: Now and then type a neighbouring key, notice, delete and retype; default false.

pace.description: Makes the flow pace itself like a person: a dwell on every page it arrives on, a thinking time between actions. Absent: no pacing.

FlowBehavior.description: How the human steps of a flow are performed, and whether the flow paces itself.

FlowEvent.description: One line of a flow's NDJSON stream, chosen by `type`.

console.text: Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 ()

error.message: the navigation did not finish within 60000 ms

result.description: The page as the flow left it.

behavior.description: What the behavior engine did over the whole flow; null when no step was a human one and the flow was not paced. Its `dwell_ms` is the sum of the dwells of a paced flow, 0 otherwise.

dwell_ms.description: Median of the time the persona stays on a page after arriving on it, before the next step. Each dwell is drawn from a log-normal with this median whose 95th percentile is twice the median. Absent: the persona's own human dwell (log-normal, median about 6 s, at most 45 s).

min_dwell_ms.description: No dwell is shorter than this; default 0. A shorter draw is drawn again, never raised to the floor, so that dwells do not pile up at it.

wander.description: Whether the persona's idle hand wanders while it dwells on a page it arrived on; default true. False: the dwell sends no input at all, the hand rests. The thinking time before a step is the same either way. Since 1.5.0.

FlowPace.description: How a flow paces itself. Present, even empty: after every step that arrived on a page (a `goto`; a `click`, `press` or `back` after which a new document or another address was seen) the persona dwells there, its idle hand wandering unless `wander` is false, before the next step. And before every step other than the five that only read (`wait_for`, `assert`, `extract`, `screenshot`, `pdf`) it takes a thinking time of its own (log-normal, median 0.4 to 0.9 s by persona, 80 ms to 5 s), unless it has just dwelled or the step is the flow's first. So no two actions are a constant time apart and none follows a read at machine speed. The reading steps are never delayed and send no input. A click or a key of the driver (`human: false`) is then watched for a navigation as a person's is (1.2 s). Every time is drawn from the stream of the flow's seed, so the same flow replays. A pause never outlasts the flow's budget less a reserve for the captures; it counts in the `duration_ms` and `paced_ms` of its step, not against the step's `timeout_ms`. Absent: the flow runs its steps one right after the other.

capture.description: What the final page result captures.

timeout_ms.description: Budget for the whole flow; default 180000.

behavior.description: How the human steps are performed.

duration_ms.description: How long the step took, its pacing included.

paced_ms.description: The part of `duration_ms` that was pacing: the thinking time before the step and the dwell after it. Null when the flow is not paced (`behavior.pace` absent).

error.description: Why the step failed; null when it did not.

capture.description: What an `extract`, `screenshot` or `pdf` step captured; null otherwise.

FlowStepEvent.description: A finished step of a flow.

seed.description: The persona's recorded seed. The same seed, constraints and sidecar build give the same fingerprint, byte for byte.

claimed_os.description: The operating system the persona claims. An engine that may not claim another system than its host's answers `cross_os_claim_disabled`.

languages.description: The persona's languages, most preferred first; the first is its locale.

browser_major.description: The browser major Kage expects the engine to bundle. When given and different from the installed browser's, the answer is `browser_major_mismatch`.

fingerprint.description: The fingerprint document. Kage stores it unchanged and sends it back on every context open; only the sidecar reads it.

summary.description: The same fingerprint in a few fields.

summary.user_agent: Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/155.0.0.0 Safari/537.36

Geolocation.description: A point the geolocation API reports once a site has been given permission.

GlMode.description: Where WebGL comes from. `none`: no WebGL. `swiftshader`: Chrome's bundled software renderer. `llvmpipe`: Mesa's software renderer through ANGLE. `host`: a GPU of the host mapped into the container.

human.description: Perform the step the way a person would (mouse path, key cadence); default true.

timeout_ms.description: Budget for this step in milliseconds; default 30000.

status.description: Always `ok`: an unhealthy server does not answer 200.

browser_version.description: Full version of the browser the engine drives, for example `155.0.8059.39`; null when the engine is a stub without a browser.

max_contexts.description: The most contexts this container opens at once (`SIDECAR_MAX_CONTEXTS`).

contract_version.description: Semantic version of the contract this server speaks.

human.description: Perform the step the way a person would (mouse path, key cadence); default true.

timeout_ms.description: Budget for this step in milliseconds; default 30000.

HoverAction.description: Move the pointer over an element.

origin.description: The origin the cookies belong to. A cookie for another site is refused.

ImportStateRequest.description: Cookies to put into a context.

rejected.description: Cookies that were refused, with the reason.

InjectMode.description: How a persisted fingerprint reaches a page. `none`: nothing is injected, launch parameters make the persona. `window`: one script built from the fingerprint runs in every document before the page (cross-OS claims only).

url.description: The page to load. `http` and `https` only. There is no referer option: a referer set by the driver leaves with `Sec-Fetch-Site: none`, a pair no real navigation has. Arriving from another page is `behavior.entry`: a link there is clicked.

timeout_ms.description: Budget for the navigation and its waits; default 60000. Without `behavior.patience_ms` it also bounds the behavior on the page.

challenge_wait_ms.description: How long a detected interstitial is given to resolve by itself; default 15000.

dwell_ms.description: Time spent on the page after the wait and before the capture; default 0. Ignored when `behavior.dwell` is `human`.

max_body_bytes.description: Largest raw body and DOM kept; default 10000000. A longer one is cut and flagged.

artifact_prefix.description: Directory below the artifacts volume for the files of this navigation; default `sidecar/<context id>`.

behavior.description: What the persona does on the page; absent for a bare page load.

NavigateRequest.description: One page load in a persona context.

net_error.description: The browser's own error name, for example `ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED`; null without one.

NavigationError.description: Why a navigation did not arrive.

NavigationErrorCode.description: Why a navigation did not arrive. `timeout`: the budget ran out. `proxy_failed`: the proxy refused, failed or could not be reached. `navigation_failed`: the browser reported a network error for the target. `aborted`: the page turned into a download or was closed, or the entry did not find its link (`behavior.entry.outcome` says so).

persona_id.description: The persona. One persona has at most one open context.

fingerprint.description: The fingerprint document exactly as `POST /v1/personas/generate` returned it.

proxy.description: The persona's proxy. Every request of the context leaves through it.

locale.description: The language of the browser's own interface, for example `de-DE`.

geolocation.description: The point the geolocation API reports once a site has permission; null to report none. The permission itself is never granted automatically.

screen.description: The persona's screen. It must equal the fingerprint's.

profile_dir.description: The persona's browser profile directory, relative to the personas volume. Created when missing; cookies, storage and history accrue in it.

OpenContextRequest.description: Everything a persona context is opened with.

context_id.description: The context. It names the context in every later call.

persona_id.description: The persona the context belongs to.

reused.description: True when the persona already had an open context with the same parameters and that one is returned.

browser_version.description: Full version of the browser that runs the context.

applied.user_agent: Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/155.0.0.0 Safari/537.36

url.description: Where it leads: the absolute address the browser resolved.

text.description: The text of the link, white space collapsed, at most 200 characters.

rel.description: The tokens of its `rel` attribute, in lower case: the first 16, each cut at 64 characters.

visible.description: Whether a reader can see it: it is rendered (not `display: none`, not `visibility: hidden`, not fully transparent, nor inside anything that is), has a box, and that box lies on the canvas of the document. A link that is not is one nobody can click.

furniture.description: Whether it stands in what a site repeats on every page: inside `nav`, `header`, `footer` or `aside`, or an element with the ARIA role of one.

PageLink.description: One link of a document, as a reader meets it.

url.description: The URL that was asked for.

final_url.description: The URL of the document when it was captured.

status.description: Status of the main response; null when there was none.

http_version.description: Protocol of the main response as the browser names it, for example `h2`.

headers.description: Headers of the main response, in order, names in lower case.

redirects.description: The redirects that were answered before the main response, in order. Kage checks every hop against its SSRF rules afterwards.

title.description: The document title; null when nothing was loaded.

dom_html.description: The document as HTML after the wait settled; null when not requested or not loaded.

raw_body.description: The body of the main response; null when not requested or not available.

xhr.description: The XHR and fetch() responses that matched the request's filter.

xhr_dropped.description: Matching responses that were not kept because the page had more than `max_responses`.

screenshot.description: The screenshot file; null without one.

pdf.description: The PDF file; null without one.

side_effects.description: Events the captures fired in the page, in order. Empty when the page could notice nothing.

error.description: Why the navigation did not arrive; null when it did. Whatever was captured is still present.

behavior.description: What the behavior engine did; null when the request asked for no behavior.

links.description: The links of the document to `http` and `https` addresses, in document order, a link that occurs twice listed twice; an address longer than a navigation takes (8192 characters) is left out. Null when not requested or nothing was loaded.

links_truncated.description: Whether the document held more links than `links` lists.

error.message: the navigation did not finish within 60000 ms

human.description: Perform the step the way a person would (mouse path, key cadence); default true.

timeout_ms.description: Budget for this step in milliseconds; default 30000.

engine.description: The engine that generated the fingerprint.

claimed_os.description: The operating system the persona claims.

browser_version.description: Full version of the installed browser.

browser_major.description: Major version of the installed browser.

hardware_concurrency.description: Logical processors the persona would report. A context reports at most the host's count.

languages.description: The persona's languages, most preferred first.

key.description: The key, as `KeyboardEvent.key` names it, for example `Enter`.

server.description: The proxy as `http://host:port`. HTTP CONNECT only.

location.description: Its `Location` header; null when it had none.

RejectedCookie.description: A cookie that was not imported.

human.description: Perform the step the way a person would (mouse path, key cadence); default true.

full_page.description: False: the visible viewport, which no page can observe. True: the whole document, which fires `resize` in the page (once or twice); the result names that side effect.

quality.description: Quality for `jpeg` and `webp`; default 80. Ignored for `png`.

ScrollEnd.description: Why the scrolling of a page ended. `depth`: the depth asked was reached. `patience`: `behavior.patience_ms` was used up first. `budget`: no patience was given and what `timeout_ms` left was used up first. `page`: the page does not scroll, or not any further. A page that grows for as long as it is scrolled ends after 400 turns of the wheel, reported as `patience` or `budget`.

selector.description: CSS selector of the select element.

human.description: Perform the step the way a person would (mouse path, key cadence); default true.

SelectAction.description: Choose an option of a select element.

id.description: Short name of the page; findings and artifacts carry it.

settle_ms.description: How long the page is given to finish its own tests after load; default depends on the kind.

weight.description: Weight of each finding of this page in the score; default 1.

rules.description: The checks of a `generic` page. Ignored for the other kinds.

SelftestPageKind.description: How a self-test page is read. `probe`: Kage's coherence probe (it publishes its findings as JSON). `echo`: Kage's fingerprint echo (TLS, HTTP/2 and header order). `sannysoft`: bot.sannysoft.com. `creepjs`: CreepJS. `generic`: any page, read with the regular expressions of the request.

http_status.description: Status of the page's main response; null without one.

duration_ms.description: How long the page took, every load and the pause between two loads included.

attempts.description: How many times the page was loaded: 2 when its first load ended in a timeout, a proxy or a network error and it was loaded once more after a short pause, and is judged by that second load. A page that arrived is never loaded again, whatever its checks say. Absent from a sidecar of before 1.6.0, which loaded every page once. Since 1.6.0.

text.description: The visible text of the page as a file, as evidence.

screenshot.description: A screenshot of the page, as evidence.

SelftestPageReport.description: What happened with one page of a self-test.

SelftestPageStatus.description: Whether a page could be used. `unreachable`: it did not load. `unparsed`: it loaded but did not look as its kind expects.

pages.description: The pages to load; default: the sidecar's configured set, which holds Kage's own pages only. Third-party pages are only ever loaded because a request names them.

echo.description: What an `echo` page must report; without it an echo page only reports what it saw.

min_score.description: The lowest score that passes; default 90.

artifact_prefix.description: Directory below the artifacts volume for the evidence files; default `sidecar/<context id>/selftest`.

SelftestRequest.description: A self-test of one persona context.

passed.description: No hard failure, and the score is at least `min_score`.

complete.description: False when a page could not be reached or read: the verdict then rests on fewer checks.

score.description: 100 × (1 − (weight of fails + half the weight of warns) / weight of all known checks); 100 when nothing is known.

SelftestResponse.description: Findings and score of a self-test.

check.description: Name of the finding this rule produces.

pattern.description: A regular expression, matched case-insensitively against the visible text of the page.

expect.description: Whether the pattern must be found or must be absent.

hard.description: Whether a failure of this rule fails the whole self-test.

SelftestRule.description: One regular-expression check of a `generic` page.

SideEffect.description: An event a capture fired in the page. `resize`: a full-page screenshot. `beforeprint` and `afterprint`: a PDF.

StorageEntry.description: One key of a web storage area.

total_ms.description: Until every wait and capture was done.

Timing.description: Milestones of a navigation in milliseconds; null for one that was not reached.

human.description: Perform the step the way a person would (mouse path, key cadence); default true.

timeout_ms.description: Budget for this step in milliseconds; default 30000.

fingerprint.description: The fingerprint document as Kage stored it: generated, or moved before, by an engine of the same kind.

UpgradePersonaRequest.description: A stored fingerprint to move to the browser major the engine's sidecar runs.

fingerprint.description: The document for the browser the engine runs: the same device and seeds, with the browser's version moved as the browser's own update moves it. The same request gives the same document, byte for byte; a document of that version comes back unchanged.

summary.description: The moved fingerprint in a few fields.

upgraded.description: Whether the document changed: false when it was of the engine’s browser already.

UpgradePersonaResponse.description: A persona fingerprint for the browser major the engine runs.

summary.user_agent: Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/155.0.0.0 Safari/537.36
Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/155.0.0.0 Safari/537.36

until.description: The lifecycle point to wait for.

selector.description: A CSS selector that must match an attached element afterwards; null or absent for none.

extra_ms.description: Milliseconds to wait after everything else; default 0.

Wait.description: What a navigation waits for before the page is captured.

selector.description: Wait until this CSS selector matches.

url.description: Wait until the URL matches this glob.

network_idle.description: Wait until no request ran for 500 ms.

human.description: Perform the step the way a person would (mouse path, key cadence); default true.

timeout_ms.description: Budget for this step in milliseconds; default 30000.

WaitForAction.description: Wait for one condition: exactly one of the four fields is set.

WaitUntil.description: When a navigation counts as arrived. `commit`: the response started. `domcontentloaded`: the document is parsed. `load`: the load event fired. `network_idle`: load, then no request for 500 ms.

content_types.description: Media types to keep, compared without parameters and case; a value ending in `/*` or `+json` style suffixes is matched as a prefix or suffix. Example: `application/json`.

max_bytes.description: Largest body kept per response; a longer body is cut and flagged.

max_responses.description: Most responses kept per page; default 100. Later ones are dropped.

XhrCapture.description: Which XHR and fetch() responses a navigation keeps.

content_type.description: The response media type, without parameters.

body.description: The response body; null when the browser no longer held it.

XhrResponse.description: One XHR or fetch() response a page received.
